item.title: Clowns (seeking greenlights): Re: Clowns (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded: Everyone but the owner of the doll believes that it is creepy, almost horrifyingly so and prefer not to be around it or they will try to get rid of it. The owner on the other hand would believe it gives them some type of protection(I haven't decided if it does or not — maybe it makes them have pleasant dreams and when removed causes nightmares of the doll's "true"/frightening appearance. I thought this might clutter so it might just not do that.) and will become violent or angry if the doll is removed or even insulted, which would be boosted by the doll's effects on strength. Testing would be done to see the range of the dolls effects, if they could be used for benefit, how the effects change over distance/if the doll was separated from the owner for a period of time (the discovery on the separation would be that if separated long enough the owner will begin to feel antsy—similar to a withdrawal situation) and also on what exactly the doll/the force behind the doll considers "ownership" (does a previous owner have to die, or is giving the doll up enough?).

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The First and Forever Prisoner: (Seeking Greenlight) The First and Forever Prisoner
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: History

Elevator Pitch: Following the history of the one we know as SCP-682 from it's birth as a child of the Scarlet King, exiled to Earth until she could kill everyone, to being an inmate in Titania's Prison, to trying to release it's father only to be imprisoned by the Keepers. The only thing stopping it from detroying the world has been the legacy of the Jailors that have kept it imprisoned for most of it's existence, the Foundation is only the most recent to inherit the role.

Central Narrative: Connecting the dots between several hints regarding 682
- born as A'zieb, the fourth child/bride of the Scarlet King
- Mal-Va-Gar-Ta-Mor, SCP-2932-A, first imprisonment under the Children of the Night and the Hudaru
- The Bastard Son of Apep, SCP-557-1, the Ancient Containment Site was actually the first version of SCP-2317, the stone in the floor of Room 501 sealing off the Scarlet King(the other door was made later when this way could not be accessed) his fourth child led an army to break his seal only to be imprisoned as well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This isn't about killing the Hard-to-Kill Reptile, this is about why it matters that it is contained by the Foundation and it's precursors. Also information on why both the Reptile and the King are not meant to be destroyed at all.

Additional Notes: I am also planning on connecting Mekhane/Wan and/or the Lord of Endowments in this story to tie it to another tale I'm working on. The Gods are critical in sealing and containing the Prisoners.

item.title: SCP-XXXX: Children of the Stars: SCP-XXXX: Children of the Stars
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: Ten individual children have their consciousness taken over by incorporeal beings and become seemingly immortal for reasons that are currently unknown.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX, which is not the children but rather what has taken control of the children's consciousness, are interviewed and studied by the researchers. During the interviews, they come to learn that they use the children in order to have a physical body in this reality and to accomplish particular rituals to appease a long overlooked god.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A possible, yet not direct relation to the Fifth Church and a connection to one of the monolithic figures depicted in one of the murals within SCP-4840.

Well, I wanted to make the story base on incidents that happened because of the SCP. This was just one of the incidents that the SCP caused.

Incident logs alone won't be able to fully carry the story, as they don't show much of an arc, much less a strong payoff. When pitching the narrative, you're looking to show a brief summary of the whole story, from the setup to the payoff and the main conflict.- its essentially a very brief draft.

The Foundation doesn't catch it because it teleports to different places around the world for another victim, but they are involved and they do learn it has a pattern of where it goes and when it strikes.

This sounds a bit off to me, if it has a pattern then the Foundation should (theoretically) be able to contain it, or at least put more permanent and/or streamlined techniques in place to contain it. Currently their containment method feels fairly makeshift and rough.

This also wasn't mentioned in the narrative pitch much, which makes it hard for me to get an idea of the draft would look like.

I didn't mean to do it in an insensitive way. I wanted to make it creepy and mysterious at the same time.

item.title: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell: Re: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for your feedback!

Eh, in my opinion, this feels more like a inspiration of SCP-513 just that the effects of the bell are more violent.

Bugger, I didn't know that one. I wonder now if this has enough to stand on it's own. I am tying it in to historical people and events, and it has different effects, so possibly.

show spoilers
hide spoilers

Honestly, the name came first (after reading Pink Floyd's wikipedia article!). Then thoughts started circulating: a bell that divides people somehow. Option 1: It actually splits them in two somehow, nah, don't like it. Option 2: The sound has an effect on their aggression (stimulates the amygdala? enhanced fight-or-flight reaction?) and causes them to attack other people. From there, I started reading up on the history of bells and how to tie it in to the SCP.
Simultaneously, while I love cool monster SCPs, I also like SCPs where there's a smidge of plausibility. I recently re-read 096 and his rage issues. What if a similar violent rage happened, but to normal people, not a superhuman impossible beastie. We'd be exhausted after a short time and likely to injure ourselves as well as others. Afterwards there would be profound psychological impacts - suicide likely.

How DID they renovate it exactly? You can't leave that blank. While the foundation does leave some stuff away, you have to give a little bit of context.

Well, this is just an ideas critique/greenlight, not a finished draft. But I imagine it's removal of tarnish, re-attachment of the clapper, suspension from a frame, addition of a rope. I might add something if I draft an article, but it's not really important.

I'd recommend you keeping it secret since some SCPs have their locations of where they were found redacted or with a black box. THAT'S what the Foundation does to keep things secret.

Eh, I'm torn on this. The SCP has been removed from the discovery location (and there's nothing anomalous about the location istself). In universe, the SCP data is only available to SCP personnel anyway. I'm not sure what benefit there would be to redacting it, there's not really a reason to keep the location secret. I don't want to redact just for the sake of it.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "The Frozen Wood": SCP-XXXX "The Frozen Wood"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale (after SCP is established)

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Class: Euclid

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX is a snowy, Birch forest varying in size, but often appears in a 10 KM x 12 KM radius. The subject seems to teleport to areas around the world at random (along with anything inside it), leaving a large, empty area in its wake, but is limited to cold climates and/or places that are experiencing severe winter storms. Strangely, the area always seems to be entirely sterile, no life can survive, be it plant, animal, bacteria, or even tardigrade!

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP tale I was planning for this follows a lone huntsman as he has unknowingly stumbled into this forest looking for game. He starts feeling weak, his vision blurry, and the snow taking on a slight red-ish hue. He starts coughing up blood, eventually too weak to go any further and contemplates his own mortality as he slowly dies in the snow. A lot of this story will have to do with what goes on in the character's mind, and how he deals with his impending death. (just a summary of the story)

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

As stated before, the forest cannot support any life whatsoever, except for the trees that grow in it; these trees, designated SCP-XXXX-A, release a toxic, spore-like pollen that sterilizes and kills all known terrestrial lifeforms (many SCP's are not affected), but thankfully, only within it's area of effect. These spores are inhaled and break down the cells of the organism, causing; internal bleeding from torn organ tissue, destruction of muscle fibers/tissue leading to paralysis, vomiting blood, asphyxiation, convulsions and/or seizures, always ending with total organ failure and death.

After tracking it for years and sending hazmat-suit equipped recovery teams into the area, a total of 247 human bodies have been discovered, as well as the corpses of wildlife native to many different regions. Strangely, these bodies were perfectly intact, no decay had occurred as there were no bacteria left to break the bodies down.

Additional Notes:

- The spores from SCP-XXXX-A cannot survive outside of SCP-XXXX's area of effect, thus, the only way to study the spores is to be within the subject itself.

- Due to its often secluded location and it's deadly nature, as long as the Foundation is careful about the spores, a well protected base could be built inside the area as well as utilizing its random teleportation effect to avoid detection by the public!

item.title: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]: Re: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your reply!

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Overall, the skip doesn't have much context around it, there's no clear motives and no clear in-universe justification for existing. Which as a result, makes the skip feel close to a "thing that does a thing", along with causing it to just feel like your average murder monster.

I do agree with you that this SCP is basically just a thing that does a thing, but I don't fully agree with the "murder monster" part. It was my fault for not fully explaining it, but the cap doesn't always want to kill people. It just wants to hurt or humiliate its victim the best way it can without killing them.

there's no reason why the skip is a cap, or why the skip specifically has these anomalies (teleportation, telepathy, etc.)

Yeah, I agree with the first part. It being a cap is kinda silly, but how it gets its anomalies was supposed to be a mystery, so it can make it interesting.

or why it's interested in tricking people.

It's not interested in tricking people. It's interested in other peoples' sorrow and will go to great lengths to torment them by making them do terrible stuff to themselves or others for something they will not get in the end. That's why it's called "a very sadistic cap." It enjoys peoples' pain and misery, and that's its motivation to why it does these things.

(EDIT: wait no, I take back. You're right, I don't know why it's interested in tricking people. Maybe I put that in there because I wanted the SCP to be a good manipulator or something.)

The Narrative:

First off, this seems much closer to a single incident rather than a narrative. As there's little to no clear arc, and most questions the concept raised are still left unanswered.

Well, I wanted to make the story base on incidents that happened because of the SCP. This was just one of the incidents that the SCP caused.

Foundation doesn't seem to be involved here at all, there isn't anything showing how they found it, what happened during its containment, and what they learned.

The Foundation doesn't catch it because it teleports to different places around the world for another victim, but they are involved and they do learn it has a pattern of where it goes and when it strikes.

The suicide note feels like a narrative device to drum up tension or make the skip seem more dangerous, which (to me at least) comes off as edgy and a bit cliched, considering how much this sort of storyline is seen in other media.

You're definitely right about this. I was trying to show how manipulative the SCP was and how it's not a thing to mess with, but the suicide note just made it edgy. I kinda cringed a bit when I read it again lol.

on a side note, suicide in general can be a rather sensitive topic, if you do wish to include it, it will need to be handled carefully.

I didn't mean to do it in an insensitive way. I was trying to make the atmosphere creepy and mysterious at the same time by using the paintings, photos, and the suicide note.

Hook:

This if fairly dull, as the skips effects or motives won't be able to carry the article alone, for this to work as a hook (IMO), they would need to be integrated and communicated effectively in the narrative (which currently they aren't). Generally speaking, you're looking to put the main idea or core narrative conflict in the hook.

I agree with this. I will try to change it soon.

Overall, this is some really good critique. Thanks!

item.title: Lost objects appear at 0°N 0°E (Greenlight): Re: Lost objects appear at 0°N 0°E (Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
1) Don't post a sandbox unless it has been specifically requested.

2) There's not much of a narrative here. You've got essentially a neat quirk that resolves some interesting questions, but it would be interesting to find out how they discovered the problem and how they determined that the objects were from that date. `Also, how it was determined that they from "unset coordinates" would be really interesting.

3) Another problem is that the items are appearing based on time coordinate problems, not geographic coordinates. While it's cool, it should be better stated.

4) You need an actual hook, not just more description. The question is why is this interesting, and how does it contribute to the universe needs to be addressed, and this is the section for that.

Cool idea; just needs some polishing.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
It's just a fact of baseline reality that this anomaly cannot be contained

This might come off as just being overpowered to force the narrative to be what the author wants. It feels more contrived than, say, SCP-1915 (Status Quo) where the anomaly is very difficult to contain, but the reality bending for that anomaly feels inherent to the character's story independent of any authorial meddling.

The overuse of resources and personnel is due to the fact that they can't get him to stay in containment for more than five minutes

My main suspension of disbelief gripe is the Foundation taking so long and using up so many resources before they figure out what they need to do. If you really want to go that route, it's your prerogative as author; however, I would not be greenlighting a premise that relies on that narrative setup.

The character can also be reduced from an arrogant parody of Mary Sues to someone who really, really doesn't want to be locked up.

This approach would be much more workable—fear of being confined is more relatable to the average reader.

item.title: Dystopan Afterlfe: Re: Dystopan Afterlfe
item.content:encoded:
You have some decent ideas, but nothing that really congeals. There is no real narrative here, and you seem to no real interest in it yourself; there's not much here but a sketch. Even your central narrative isn't more than just an incident and it barely counts as that.

You need to flesh out the pocket dimension: How is it accessed, how does MC&D have control over it, how often do they use it, etc. Also, some sample tortures would be great, as well as some description of the dimension itself.

Also, you might want to drop the 05s reference unless you plan on building on it. Otherwise, it just seems like a weird shot.

You have an interesting skeleton; now flesh it out.

item.title: Buzzcut: Re: Buzzcut
item.content:encoded:
In all honesty, you would do almost better to make this a -J; with a little more framing, this would make a decent joke SCP.

I sort of like the idea of a buzzer that creates such an impressive haircut that it can create a new idol; it has a very anime feel to it. The right buzzer could create some interesting results, especially if the person was a demagogue to begin with.

That said, you need to beef up the lore of the buzzer a bit; its history should not begin and end with Elvis, but add on other people. A few politicians, famous speakers, etc., would round this one out very nicely, especially if you showed a fall from grace or two that was because they stopped shaving.

You can also have it stolen not by someone just wanting to resell but by someone planning on using it for nefarious purposes, or even just getting laid.

You have a great idea. Now have some fun with it!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the criticism. I still think that this can work, if I change the premise enough:

The "Foundation being incompetent" thing isn't a necessary part of the article, and can be rewritten by making our anomaly a semiohazard, a fact of the universe that shouldn't be true, but is. It's just a fact of baseline reality that this anomaly cannot be contained, just as it is a fact of baseline reality that "The operations of 'YWTGTSYT' are perfectly legal." The overuse of resources and personnel is due to the fact that they can't get him to stay in containment for more than five minutes – and that also applies to the trucks they use to transport him. And while it would make more sense to convince the guy to remain in containment or keep him comatose, the first is not going to happen unless they threaten lethal force (which is what they figure out they have to do) for reasons discussed below, and the second counts as "containment" and thus will not work.

The character can also be reduced from an arrogant parody of Mary Sues to someone who really, really doesn't want to be locked up. He's had nightmares about it, he's always been terrified of it, and getting sentenced to prison confirmed all his worst fears about it. The causal link between this fear and the manifestation of his anomaly is unconfirmed; perhaps this was always a property of him, but it never became an issue until he was carted off to jail. Perhaps he manifested the property after going to jail.

Do you think that could work?
